_comment: Who does which job. Each role lists workers in order; dispatch.ps1 takes the first one that is not frozen. `model` is a key of that worker's `models`. Cursor model names are never listed: `effort` (low|medium|high) plus the worker's `family` (a name fragment, the one thing to edit when the plan changes) pick the newest matching model from `agent models` at dispatch; if none matches, Cursor `auto`. Policy: implement = medium, implement-strong, architect and review = high. A reviewer is never the worker that wrote the PR (the Claude review run is a different worker from Cursor/DeepSeek authors; a DeepSeek or Cursor review of the other's PR is future work). Intent labels: GitHub issues carry an intent (`architect`, `implement`, `review`), never a worker; the router maps intent -> role -> worker. The old `cursor`/`deepseek` labels are gone; the router alone picks the worker (freezes, schedule, availability). Workers with `dispatchable: false` are skipped by dispatch.ps1 (Claude architect work is not started by it yet, so architect issues go to the next worker). `schedule.freeze` freezes a worker automatically (times in `schedule.timezone`); it is separate from the manual FREEZE files. DeepSeek peak pricing (2x) is 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday-Friday, except Chinese public holidays (list those dates in `offPeakDates`): https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing

filters.stage1_relevant: task label (architect|implement), or PR with a new head, or owner comment; not closed, pinned or `later`
filters.stage2_claimable: no marker for this issue/head, worker not frozen, no worker already running, budget not spent
